statement: Which of these numbers leaves remainder 2 when divided by 5?

choices.misconception: I picked a multiple of five, which leaves no remainder at all.
I picked another multiple of five rather than a number two past one.
I picked a number three past a multiple of five rather than two.
I picked a multiple of five and read the 2 in the number as the remainder.

hints: Look for a number two more than a multiple of five.
Multiples of five end in 0 or 5, so a number leaving remainder 2 ends in 2 or 7. Check the last digit of each choice rather than dividing them all out.
32 is 30 + 2, and 30 is a multiple of five.

solutions.reliable: A number leaves remainder 2 on division by 5 exactly when it is two more than a multiple of 5, which means it ends in 2 or 7. Only 32 does. The transferable idea: convert a remainder condition into a condition on the last digit, which turns five divisions into one glance.

whyOnTest: Reading a digit of the number as the remainder is the standard confusion, and that answer is on the list.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
